sections.title: A scale of adverbs
sections.content: You know stance adverbs such as *francamente* and *indudablemente*, with their commas, from B2 Unit 1, and *probablemente* and *posiblemente* from B1 Unit 22. Here is the whole scale of adverbs of probability, from less sure to more sure, and the mood each one takes.

sections.title: From less sure to more sure
rows: a lo mejor, quizás, tal vez
maybe: it could be, or not
most likely; it does not mean 'certainly'

sections.title: Which mood?
sections.content: *A lo mejor*, *seguramente* and *sin duda* are followed by the indicative. *Quizás* and *tal vez* take either mood, as in Lesson 1. After *probablemente* and *posiblemente* the indicative is the usual choice: *Probablemente llega mañana*. The subjunctive is also possible when the adverb opens the sentence, and it adds a touch of doubt. If you are unsure, the indicative is the safe choice with these two.

sections.title: Position, and a different kind of adverb
sections.content: As with the stance adverbs of B2 Unit 1, these adverbs can open the sentence, sit between commas or close it: *Seguramente, Marta ya ha salido.* / *Marta, seguramente, ya ha salido.* / *Marta ya ha salido, seguramente.* *Por lo visto* 'apparently' is different: it does not say how likely you think something is, it says that you know it from what you saw or heard.

items.spanish: Seguramente Marta ya ha salido de la oficina.
items.english: Marta has most likely left the office already.

items.spanish: Sin duda, es la mejor opción.
items.english: Without doubt, it is the best option.

items.spanish: Posiblemente tiene razón, pero no estoy seguro.
items.english: She is possibly right, but I am not sure.

items.spanish: Por lo visto, Pablo cambió de trabajo.

items.english: Marta has already left, most likely.

sections.content: *Seguramente* is closer to English 'most likely' than to 'surely' or 'certainly'. For certainty, use *sin duda*. One marker is enough for a guess: *seguramente a lo mejor* sounds heavy.
